sentences.text: The fossil record of Yuanmousaurus consists of nine dorsal vertebrae, three sacral vertebrae, and seven caudal vertebrae.
Measurements indicate the humerus was 0.72 times the length of the femur.
The single known specimen, catalogued as YMV 601, was collected in May 2000 from the village of Jiangyi in Yunnan Province.
Lü Junchang and colleagues formally named the species Yuanmousaurus jiangyiensis in 2006.
This animal lived approximately 165 million years ago during the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic in Asia.
Other estimates place its existence between 174.7 and 161.5 million years ago, spanning the Aalenian to Callovian stages.
Many paleontologists have abandoned the family Euhelopodidae because the systematic position of Euhelopus is controversial.
It is debated whether Yuanmousaurus is a valid genus, as it may be considered dubious.
